open_issues.summary: Ordinary ADS input leaves the AK-74M at hip composition

blocking_focus: Ordinary traversal deadlocks before Alpha capture, leaving the required Bravo and Charlie enemy groups inactive.
Two short player-fire inputs consume four AK-74M rounds instead of two.
The ADS sample retains the hip composition, and the complete enemy hurt/death plus third-person victory motion chain is unavailable.
Authoritative enemy damage has a red direction arc but no synchronized visible enemy muzzle, tracer, or impact result in the matched frame.
The victory and detonation terminal presentation chains are absent.
Escape remains deterministically multiply bound to pause and menu_back in project.godot.
A large calibration target remains in the central shipped gameplay sightline.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Make player and enemy combat feedback exact-once, readable, and production-presentable, then implement the complete authoritative bomb success and detonation presentations while preserving the intact map, viewmodels, enemy roster, checkpoint behavior, HUD components, and clean boot.

diagnosis.root_cause: Combat feedback lacks single-source event ownership across input and presentation. Player press/release authority is reconstructed from frame-polled InputMap state, so short raw-event windows can remain held long enough for the AUTO scheduler to commit an extra round. Enemy attacks commit ammo, damage, and directional HUD state, but the shipped scene does not bind the same shot ID to a readable muzzle, tracer, impact, and audio chain. The production main scene also directly instances a calibration target, while product-owned daylight settings flatten pale authored-map materials.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, extract, duplicate, reposition, or edit authored children of the preserved Standoff environment.
Do not split or reconstruct the preserved AK-74M/Saiga-12 hands-and-viewmodel packages.
Do not change the verified 18 enemy identities or 3/5/10 regional distribution.
Do not create work for deferred issues or backlog gaps in this iteration.
Do not claim completion from source inspection, node names, particle counts, or UI dictionaries; host/Tester must obtain the specified current-candidate state, frame, and audio/VFX evidence.
If terminal video is unavailable, use the PRD-permitted coherent still fallback with functional timing and skip behavior; do not block, show black output, or fabricate a video claim.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different strategy for the repeated fire defect: replace frame-state edge reconstruction with one timestamped normalized input-event stream, and make AUTO cadence consume only its explicit held interval. Bind combat sensory channels to immutable shot events through an idempotent presenter. Keep the bomb finale as a separate terminal observer of authoritative mission state so cinematic callbacks cannot create, duplicate, or delay results.

code: Parse/load every edited GDScript and scene with no missing resources, invalid NodePaths, duplicate class names, or new errors.
Confirm one normalized raw-event path owns fire press/release and that AUTO scheduling cannot create an independent press or extend beyond recorded release time.
Confirm combat and terminal presenters deduplicate immutable event IDs and clear bounded caches on checkpoint, replay, and home transitions.
Confirm the production main-scene dependency graph no longer contains BallisticsCalibrationPlate or another exposed calibration substitute.
runtime: Host/Tester combat input matrix: fresh AK-74M at 30 rounds; perform two sub-interval mouse taps and two sub-interval gamepad taps. Each sequence must yield exactly two accepted presses, two unique shot IDs, and 30→28 ammunition. Repeat SEMI tap, AUTO hold/release, pause-held, reload-held, switch-held, restore-held, and terminal-held cancellation cells.

Host/Tester enemy-shot matrix: capture aim window, muzzle/fire, tracer/projectile, resolved impact, and damage onset in adjacent frames for one hit; align actor ID, shot ID, enemy ammo, player health, directional arc, camera response, and decoded audio/VFX onset. Repeat a miss or blocked case with no health loss.

Host/Tester finale success matrix: through ordinary A→B→C gameplay, capture legal final-stage submission above zero, terminal event, combat freeze, safe bomb, collision-free third-person pullback, operator-facing victory dance, skip/completion, full result metrics, leaderboard write, Replay, and clean subsequent deployment.

Host/Tester finale failure matrix: through ordinary gameplay, reach countdown zero and align terminal event, one lethal damage commit, health-zero frame, control/collision shutdown, flash, expansion layers, camera-down state, red-effect lifetime, audio tail, terminal media/fallback, failure result, and restart/home actions. Debug setters and teleportation do not count as acceptance evidence.
visual: At 1280×720, capture the prior spawn framing without the calibration target plus spawn/A/B/C daylight views showing readable pale materials and contact detail.
Capture one enemy-hit adjacent-frame sequence where muzzle/tracer/impact remains readable with the damage arc and does not obscure the reticle, enemy silhouette, objective, or weapon.
Capture distinct failure frames for flash, expanding explosion, camera-down/red treatment, media/fallback, and failure result; reject full-screen red/black concealment or a label-only finale.
Capture success frames for safe bomb, third-person pullback, complete operator, victory dance, and result transition; a result label without the camera/character sequence fails.

done_when: Two sub-interval mouse taps and two sub-interval gamepad taps each produce exactly two accepted edge receipts, two unique shot commits, and magazine 30→28; no round is committed after release.

SEMI submits exactly one shot per press; AUTO submits immediately, repeats only at its configured cadence while held, and cancels on release, reload, switch, pause, death, defusal, restore, or terminal transition.

A real enemy hit exposes one shared actor/shot ID across aim telegraph, enemy ammo consumption, fire pose/recoil, visible muzzle flash, tracer/projectile, impact or near-player result, spatial shot/impact audio, health loss, directional arc, and camera response within two rendered frames.
Enemy miss and blocked cases retain event-bound muzzle/tracer/world feedback without changing health or fabricating a damage arc.
BallisticsCalibrationPlate and other calibration-only surfaces are absent from shipped gameplay while real player and enemy impact feedback remains functional.
Player/enemy shot listeners are idempotent by event ID; effect and audio lifetimes are bounded and reset on checkpoint, replay, and home transitions.

Late-morning lighting preserves the intact map and PBR materials while pale concrete and metal retain highlight texture, contact shadows, objective readability, and enemy silhouettes at spawn, A, B, and C.

The combat feedback family is production-grounded rather than debug-like: family_id `combat_event_feedback`; PRD style is warm weapon energy, amber-red enemy threat, material-aware impacts, and neutral daylight; source quality is production-eligible candidate-owned VFX/audio or Developer-selected production assets; material/texture evidence must show native transparency or additive rendering and !
tasks.instructions: Make raw input events the sole press/release authority, retaining event timestamp and source so brief mouse and gamepad windows cannot be extended by physics polling. Drive the immediate AUTO shot and later cadence from that one held interval. Route each authoritative enemy attack into one shipped, shot-ID-idempotent feedback presenter using the actual enemy muzzle and resolved endpoint; presentation observes but never creates ammo, damage, health, or score. Complete the changed combat event chain with distinct mechanical, shot, near-miss, impact, and damage cues plus bounded muzzle/tracer/impact effects. Remove the calibration target from the production main scene rather than obscuring it. Adjust only product-owned environment/lighting resources to restore neutral exposure. For the repeated combat feedback family, require at least four meaningful source/runtime variants across muzzle, tracer/projectile, character hit, and surface impact roles; material-specific variants must cover concrete/metal and character response, no single variant should exceed 40% of high-frequency visible uses, and diversity must come from effect geometry/material/audio/timing rather than palette-only changes. Use native transparent RGBA or additive VFX backgrounds, inspect actual runtime bindings, and capture spawn, combat-hit, blocked/miss, and pale-material views.
tasks.title: Repair exact-once combat feedback and production presentation

done_when: The mission controller remains the sole terminal authority, commits countdown before final defusal submission, gives zero-time detonation priority, and emits exactly one immutable terminal event ID.
Detonation sets player health to zero exactly once and disables input, attack, interaction, navigation, and blocking collision before presentation listeners run.

The same detonation event sequences flash and initial camera impulse at 0–120 ms; fireball, sparks, debris, pressure wave, dust, local lighting, bounded camera drop/tilt, red directional treatment, low-frequency blast, and audio tail at 120–650 ms; then decay before media/result entry.

The detonation camera does not teleport, clip through the floor, or restore to spawn. Reduced-motion, screen-shake, flash, red-treatment, particle-density, rumble, and volume settings reduce presentation independently without removing the health-zero/death/result truth.

Death video starts only after at least 1.5 seconds of native explosion presentation; a 4–8 second video or coherent matched still fallback supports skip/completion, after which the failure result offers earned score, recent history, replay, legal checkpoint restart, and return home.

Successful final-stage submission with remaining_time>0 makes the bomb visibly safe, freezes combat, performs a collision-safe third-person pullback, frames the operator facing the camera, plays a real skippable victory dance, and only then enters the result.

The success result shows completion and remaining time, score components, A/B state, eliminations, deaths, restart count, fastest-success delta, and leaderboard rank; failure cannot overwrite fastest-success data.

Replay, restart, and home clear terminal media, camera overrides, particles, dynamic lights, audio voices, and terminal event caches; three repeated terminal transitions do not duplicate damage, results, or listeners.
tasks.instructions: Implement one bounded terminal-presentation sequencer that observes the immutable mission terminal event but cannot submit or delay mission truth. Build separate success and failure branches. Failure must perform the complete lethal explosion, camera-down, damage-treatment, terminal-media/fallback, and failure-result sequence. Success must perform safe-bomb state, third-person pullback, real victory motion, complete score/leaderboard result, and skip handling. Every explosion layer shares one event ID and world origin, has a bounded lifetime/concurrency cap, respects accessibility controls, and cleans up on replay or restart. Treat the terminal explosion as one justified semantic singleton family: family_id `bomb_terminal_sequence`, grounded military-industrial PRD style, production-quality layered materials/audio with inspected runtime bindings, one authored composite runtime sequence, maximum single-variant share 1.0, additive or native-transparent effects, and evidence views for flash, expansion, camera-down, media/fallback, victory pullback, dance, and result.
